brief.topic: The Same Two Operations Can Lead Somewhere Else

s01: Stretch sideways, then turn. Is that the same as turning, then stretching?
Start with the point one, one. A sideways stretch doubles only its horizontal coordinate.
Stretch first. The point becomes two, one.
Now rotate a quarter turn counterclockwise. It becomes minus one, two.
Reset to the same starting point.
Rotate first. One, one becomes minus one, one.
Then stretch sideways. The result is minus two, one. Same ingredients, different destination.
Matrices record these operations. The rightmost matrix acts first on a column vector.
Rotation after stretch is R S. Stretch after rotation is S R. They are different here.
Now stretch both directions equally instead.
Doubling every coordinate before or after the turn gives minus two, two.
Some transformations commute, and others do not. Order matters because operations act on the state the previous operation leaves behind.

scenes.narration:
Stretch sideways, then turn. Is that the same as turning, then stretching? Start with the point one, one. A sideways stretch doubles only its horizontal coordinate.

Stretch first. The point becomes two, one. Now rotate a quarter turn counterclockwise. It becomes minus one, two.

Reset to the same starting point. Rotate first. One, one becomes minus one, one. Then stretch sideways. The result is minus two, one. Same ingredients, different destination.

Matrices record these operations. The rightmost matrix acts first on a column vector. Rotation after stretch is R S. Stretch after rotation is S R. They are different here.

Now stretch both directions equally instead. Doubling every coordinate before or after the turn gives minus two, two. Some transformations commute, and others do not. Order matters because operations act on the state the previous operation leaves behind.
